How Freestone County, Texas Tax Sales

Freestone County, Texas, holds tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes and put properties back into productive use. These auctions are an opportunity for buyers to invest in real estate while following Texas legal guidelines.

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course
 

When and Where

Tax sales are held on the first Tuesday of every month at 10:00 a.m. on the steps of the Freestone County Courthouse. Arrive early to confirm listings and updates. Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions.

Participation Requirements

To bid, you must register in advance. Bring a valid driver’s license or state-issued ID for verification. Payment is due immediately after the auction and must be in cash or cashier’s checks—personal checks are not accepted.

Key Details to Know

Property Condition and Research:

  • Properties are sold “as is” with no warranties or guarantees.
  • Research properties using the Freestone County Appraisal District to verify condition, location, and value.
  • Investigate any liens or encumbrances that might remain after purchase.

Click Here to Book a Call with Dustin Hahn
 

Redemption Rights:

Former owners can reclaim properties within a redemption period.

  • Non-homestead properties: 6 months.
  • Homestead or agricultural properties: Up to 2 years.

Redemption requires repayment of the purchase price plus penalties.

Unsold Properties:

Properties not sold at the auction are transferred to taxing entities as “struck-off properties.”

These may be available for sale later through other methods, such as sealed bids.

Preparing for the Auction

Understand the auction rules thoroughly, including registration deadlines and payment policies. Visit properties in person, if possible, to assess their condition. Be aware of post-purchase responsibilities like addressing title issues or repairs. Consult a real estate attorney if you’re new to tax sales.
